title: Consolidated trace/metric ingestion and burn-rate escalation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a resilient observability pipeline and on-call escalation flow that ties high-fidelity tracing hooks, multi-source metric normalization, and log enrichment into a single SLO-driven burn-rate and anomaly escalation playbook. Scope includes: (1) instrumenting lightweight tracing hooks at gateway and model-router layers to capture request route, model-variant, and KV-cache hit metadata; (2) normalizing metrics from Prometheus, frontend RUM, and runtime counters into a common schema; (3) creating a compact rolling-window anomaly detector tuned for sequence-length correlated latency spikes; (4) implementing tiered burn-rate alerts that map to paging policies and automated mitigations (fallback model variant, regional routing); and (5) delivering latency/error dashboards and an SRE playbook with runbooks and postmortem templates.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Initial discovery: Spike showed gateway-level traces lacked model-variant label. Agreed on minimal tracing hook shape: {route, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, kv_cache_hit, tenant_id}. Added to spec doc (Confluence: /display/OBS/Trace+Hook+Spec).

2025-02-15 - Trade-off discussion in eng sync: high-cardinality labels (tenant_id + prompt_hash) would blow retention costs. Decision: use tenant_id and hashed prompt bucket (8-bit) to approximate cardinality while keeping index size manageable.

2025-02-20 - Prototype implemented: lightweight hook added to model-router, emits OTLP spans with custom attributes. Performance microbench: median additional latency 0.6ms, p99 +2.2ms in worst-case. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1842

2025-02-25 - Metrics normalization: ETL job created to map prometheus counter names to unified schema (redwood.*). Identified mismatch where frontend RUM p95 is compute-time + network; normalized field added 'client_observed' vs 'server_processing'.

2025-02-28 - Burn-rate policy prototype: Two-tier burn-rate windows (5m short-window, 1h sustained). Short-window triggers automated fallback (to quantized variant) and Slack infra-alert; sustained window pages SRE. Policy stored in config service and feature-flagged behind 'slo-burn-v2'.

2025-03-03 - Anomaly detector tuning: initial detector was noisy around regional deploys. Tuned seasonal baseline using deploy-aware exclusion windows and sequence-length stratification. False-positive rate reduced from 12% -> 3% on last two weeks of test traffic.

2025-03-04 - Design review feedback from PM (Lena Hoffmann): add customer-impact mapping for enterprise tenants to skip auto-fallback; plan to expose per-tenant SLO overrides in console. Action: add auth check and UI flagging.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks emitted for 95% of production routes with required attributes
Normalized metrics pipeline populates unified metric namespace within 2 minutes of ingestion
Burn-rate alerts fire at configured thresholds and trigger automated fallback for short-window breaches
Anomaly detector tuned to <5% false-positive rate on validation traffic and excludes deploy windows
Dashboard surfaces per-route p50/p95/p99, error taxonomy, and burn-rate heatmap; runbook created and linked
